text.p: German metal and engineering sector employers federation Gesamtmetall on Wednesday proposed a so-called working time "corridor" laying down working weeks of between 30 and 40 hours.

Gesamtmetall said in a statement such contracts would be agreed by firms with individual workers. The contracts would further be on the basis that employees were then paid according to the number of hours they worked, a spokesman added.

The employers group however said it would be offering "full resistance" to the shortened work-hours proposals made by trade union IG Metall at an employment conference last week, where the union called for a 32-hour working week.

Under the IG Metall plan, the working week in the metal and engineering sectors would be reduced from the current 35 hours to 32 hours. Salaries would fall as a result, but not to the same extent as the cut in working hours.
IG Metall chief Klaus Zwickel, who made the proposal, envisages that the plan could be part-financed by the German Federal Labour Office, who would be making savings on unemployment costs.
The scheme suggested by Gesamtmetall is part of its drive to make the collective bargaining system in Germany more flexible.
"We want to offer as wide a possible contractual framework of between 30 to 40 hours that can be tailored by negotiators within firms, Gesamtmetall president Werner Stumpfe said in the statement.

Referring to IG Metall chief Klaus Zwickel's call for four-day weeks for individual workers, he added: "Four-day weeks are also possible (within such a corridor) but only if the firm is able to continue production over six days."
Gesamtmetall and IG Metall, which has some 2.7 million members, are currently holding a series of meeting to discuss a possible reform of the collective bargaining process.
